newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian president-elect insists on early poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian president-elect insists on early poll.

text.p: Bulgarian president-elect Petar Stoyanov said on Sunday talks between the government and opposition to end a deepening political crisis would be possible only if the government agreed to a general election.

Hundreds of cars flying blue opposition flags headed into Sofia from provincial towns for a rally on the seventh straight day of protests. Thousands of demonstrators surrounded the Socialist party headquarters.

"I am appealing to the ruling party and the opposition to sit at the table for talks. This is now possible only if the Bulgarian Socialist Party goes to the talks having already decided to hold early parliamentary elections," Stoyanov said in a statement.
The election of opposition lawyer Stoyanov last November marked the start of a wave of opposition to the ex-communist Socialists, who are blamed for severe economic hardship.

Thousands of protesters of all ages streamed into Sofia by car, bus and tram. Cars arriving from the provinces were greeted by a Gypsy orchestra and escorted by police to the rally site in front of the gold-domed Alexander Nevsky cathedral.
The opposition has vowed to hold daily protests until its demand for early elections is met.
